title: Yusuf and the Seed of Hope
description: A nurturing story that teaches children patience, caring for plants, and good akhlaq.

pages.text: Yusuf was a kind boy who loved nature and helping his parents. One bright morning, his father gave him a small golden seed and said, "This is a blessed seed, my son. Plant it, take care of it, and it will teach you a great secret."

Yusuf dug gently into the earth and placed the seed inside. Then he covered it with soil and watered it with sweet water. Every morning, he waited beside it, hoping the little plant would sprout quickly—but the earth stayed still.

Yusuf felt sad and went to his father, wanting to give up. His father laughed and patted his shoulder. "Yusuf, planting is like tarbiyah—both need patience, rifq, and trust in Allah. Keep watering it, and leave the rest to the Creator."

After days of care, patience, and du'a, Yusuf saw a tiny green shoot pushing through the earth, rising toward the morning sun. He was so happy! He knew now that every good deed needs patience to bloom and bear fruit.

Anas hurried home and brought back a bowl of clean water and a clean cloth. He approached the cat gently, offering the water. Then he carefully wiped its wet fur until the little cat felt safe and warm.

The little cat looked up at Anas with shining eyes and began to purr softly, showing its happiness and gratitude. Anas’s heart filled with joy because he had practiced a great virtue that Allah and His Messenger ﷺ love.

title: Layla and Her Little Star
description: A gentle story to help children relax and praise Allah for the day's blessings before sleep.

pages.text: Layla was a little girl who loved gazing at the sky before bedtime. In her cozy room, she opened the window and looked up at the clear sky filled with stars. She whispered, 'Oh shining stars of the sky, do you sleep like we do?'

A small star twinkled on the horizon, seeming to smile at Layla. She sat on her soft bed and remembered her mother’s advice: 'Layla, before you close your eyes, remember three beautiful things that happened today and thank Allah for them.'
The little star twinkled even more gently, as if inviting Layla to imagine a peaceful journey with it above the soft, silver clouds, to learn how quiet and calm fill the hearts of little ones.

Layla felt deep gratitude to Allah, who created this vast and wondrous universe and guarded it with its shining stars. She felt in her heart the greatness of the Creator and His mercy for all His servants.

Layla’s mind returned to her warm bed, and she began counting her three blessings with a smile: first, playing with her sweet kitten; second, helping her grandfather water the garden; and third, her mother’s delicious and warm food.
Layla felt complete peace. She recited Ayat al-Kursi and the du'a for sleep, then snuggled under her warm blanket and closed her eyes, seeing her little star shining softly far away.

title: Saleh and the Little Bird of Amanah
description: An engaging story that teaches children to return trusts to their owners and the importance of honesty and amanah (trustworthiness).

pages.text: One day, Saleh was playing with his ball in the neighborhood garden when he saw a little bird building its nest in a blessed olive tree. Suddenly, something shiny fell from the hand of a man passing under the tree.

Saleh ran quickly toward the tree and found a small wallet full of money. He thought for a moment: *I wonder who this wallet belongs to? I must find its owner quickly—amanah is a trait loved by Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.*

Saleh politely and gently asked the kind garden guard and his neighbor, Uncle Ahmad, if they knew the owner of the lost wallet. Everyone could see how eager he was to return the amanah to its rightful owner.
After a few steps, Saleh saw a man searching anxiously and sadly at the other end of the garden. He looked tired and worried as he rummaged through the grass, looking for something he had lost.

Saleh approached the man with gentle manners and asked him about the features of his lost wallet to be sure. When the man described it correctly, Saleh took it out and handed it to him with a warm smile.

The man’s face lit up with joy, and he prayed for Saleh’s blessings and goodness, saying, *‘Thank you for your amanah, my son.’* Saleh returned home happy, knowing that keeping amanah brings Allah’s pleasure and the love of all people.

title: Noor and the Clean Garden

Noor worked alone at first, full of energy. She put up a small wooden sign at the garden’s entrance, writing in her pretty handwriting: "Our environment is an *amanah*—let’s keep it clean and beautiful together."

Noor’s friends in the neighborhood saw what she was doing. They hurried to help her, bringing extra tools and saying, "We want our garden to be the prettiest!" Everyone worked together with team spirit and love.

To make the garden even more beautiful, the children teamed up to plant a small, colorful flower in the middle of the garden. They watered it carefully and hoped it would grow and bloom quickly to bring joy to those who passed by.

The children sat on the wooden bench, enjoying the lovely view and the gentle breeze. Noor felt proud and happy because, by working together, they had made their playground clean, beautiful, and healthy for everyone.

title: Maryam and the Toy Box
description: A gentle story that shows children the joy of sharing toys with others and making friends happy.

pages.text: On her birthday, Maryam got a new toy box filled with colourful dolls and little cars. She was so happy with her new toys, hugging them with love and great delight.

Their little neighbour Fatimah came to visit. She looked at the new toys with longing, wishing she could play with them. But Maryam hesitated, afraid her favourite toys might break, so she hid them behind her back.
Maryam stood there, unsure. She looked at Fatimah, who sat sadly beside the closed box. Maryam wondered to herself if hiding her toys was the right thing to do—would it make her friend happy?

Maryam’s mother noticed what was happening. She came closer and said gently, "Maryam, toys are more fun when we play with them together. Generosity and sharing joy bring Allah’s pleasure and make hearts happy." Maryam thought about it and decided to share.

Maryam’s heart felt at ease. She opened her wooden box and invited Fatimah, saying, "Let’s play together!" They took out the colourful blocks and started building a tall, beautiful tower, laughing out loud.

Fatimah’s face lit up with a smile, and they had a wonderful time. Maryam learned that sharing doubles the joy, makes others happy, and builds the strongest, most beautiful friendships—filling life with happiness and blessings.

title: Umar and the Light of Salah
description: An iman-filled tarbiyah story that teaches children the importance of perfecting wudu and preserving salah in its time with passion and khushu'.

pages.text: Umar was a lively child who loved playing in his garden with his friends. In the middle of their play, he heard the adhan echoing sweetly across the sky: 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar.' Umar stopped at once and looked at his friends with a smile.

He remembered that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the deeds most beloved to Allah, and he answered that it is prayer on time. Umar said to his friends, 'My friends, the call of the Creator is more important than any play. Let’s go to the masjid to pray together.'

Umar hurried to the wudu area and performed wudu slowly and carefully: washing his hands, rinsing his mouth and nose, washing his face and arms, wiping his head and ears, and washing his feet, remembering that wudu washes away sins and brightens the face with light and barakah.

Umar stood in the first row in the masjid beside his father, feeling the greatness of standing before Allah, the Most High. He performed his salah with steadiness and khushu', without rushing, reciting the Qur'an with a present heart.

After the salah ended, Umar felt a peace and tranquility fill his chest. He realized that salah is not just movements—it is a light that brightens the Muslim’s day and a great pillar that brings him closer to his Lord.
When Umar returned to his friends in the garden, he lovingly invited them to join him in performing salah always. The friends all pledged to respond immediately to the light of the adhan every time.

title: Khadijah and the Right of the Neighbor
description: A warm Islamic story that teaches children the virtue of ihsan (kindness) to neighbors, sharing food and affection, following the Prophetic Sunnah.

pages.text: On a cold evening, Khadijah was helping her mother prepare a warm, delicious soup that filled the air with a lovely smell. When the cooking was done, her mother took a big plate and said, 'Khadijah, prepare this plate for our neighbor, Grandma Aisha.'

Khadijah looked surprised and said, 'Mama, are we sending them food when they have their own?' Her mother smiled and said, 'My dear, our noble Prophet ﷺ taught us, saying: *O Abu Dharr, if you cook a broth, increase its water and look after your neighbors.*'

Khadijah carried the warm plate carefully and knocked softly on Grandma Aisha’s door. The old lady opened the door, and when she saw Khadijah with the warm plate, her face lit up with joy and happiness.
Grandma Aisha prayed for Khadijah’s blessings and success, gently patting her head. She gave her a piece of candy to thank her for her kindness and care.

Khadijah returned home with her heart dancing with happiness. She learned that Islamic law gives neighbors a great right, and that a simple, kind gift brings hearts closer and plants love in the community.
The next day, Grandma Aisha sent Khadijah a plate full of fresh fruits with a sweet thank-you note, teaching Khadijah that exchanging gifts between neighbors brings love and blessings.

title: Abdullah and 'Bismillah'
description: A warm tarbiyah story that gently shows the Sunnah manners of eating and drinking—saying 'Bismillah,' using the right hand, and praising Allah.

pages.text: Abdullah sat at the lunch table, hungry after a busy school day. The table was filled with delicious food—everything looked so good. He quickly reached out with his left hand to grab a piece of fruit.

His father stopped him gently and said, "Abdullah, do you remember the advice of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the young boy?" Abdullah immediately remembered the Prophet's ﷺ advice: to say Bismillah, eat with his right hand, and eat from what is in front of him.

Abdullah smiled, pulled his hand back, and said in a clear voice, "Bismillah." Then he began to eat with his right hand, taking food from what was in front of him—calmly and politely, without rushing or wasting.

As they ate, his father told him that saying 'Bismillah' keeps the Shaytan away and brings barakah (blessing) to the food. Eating with the right hand follows the example of the noble Prophet ﷺ and shows good Islamic manners.
When Abdullah was full, he wiped his hands and said, "Alhamdulillah." He felt content, knowing that the small Sunnahs are beautiful habits that Allah loves.
Saying 'Bismillah' and 'Alhamdulillah' became a beautiful habit for Abdullah at every meal. And every day, barakah and happiness filled the table of his kind family.

title: Aisha and the Adab of Isti'dhan
description: An Islamic tarbiyah story that teaches children the akhlaq of seeking permission and preserving the privacy of homes, following the Qur'anic guidance.

pages.text: At midday, while Aisha's mother was resting in her room, Aisha wanted to go in to get her reading book. She ran and raised her hand to push the door suddenly.

Aisha remembered her father’s words when they had memorized together the words of Allah: ﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَبۡلُغُواْ ٱلۡحُلُمَ مِنكُمۡ ثَلَٰثَ مَرَّـٰتٖ﴾. Interpretation of the meaning: 'O believers, let those in your service and your children who have not yet reached maturity ask your permission at three times.'
Aisha stood calmly at the door, knocked three gentle and polite knocks, and said in a clear, sweet voice: 'Assalamu alaykum, may I come in, Mama?'
Her mother gave permission with a warm smile and said, 'Come in, my dear. May Allah bless you and your adab.' So Aisha entered with dignity and joy.

Her mother taught Aisha that young children ask permission before coming in at three times: before the dawn prayer, at the midday rest, and after the night prayer — and that asking permission keeps everyone at home comfortable and increases the love between them.
Aisha always sought permission before entering any room or house, and she became a role model for her sisters and friends in practicing the beautiful akhlaq of isti'dhan.

pages.text: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'And Yunus was one of the messengers.' Allah sent him to his people. He called them, but they did not believe; he warned them of punishment, but they did not turn back to Allah.
He did not stay patient with them as Allah had commanded him, and he left them, angry with them, distressed by their disobedience. And he boarded a ship full of passengers and goods.

At sea, great waves surrounded the ship. The passengers drew lots to lighten its load, fearing they would drown, and the lot went against Yunus. So he was cast into the sea, and the whale swallowed him.

In the darkness of the night, the sea and the belly of the whale, Yunus called out to his Lord, repenting and admitting that he had done wrong by not staying patient with his people: ﴿لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'There is no god but You; glory be to You! I have been one of the wrongdoers.' Had it not been for his much worship and glorification of Allah, he would have stayed in the belly of the whale until the Day of Resurrection.

Allah answered his du'a and saved him from distress, and cast him out of the whale's belly onto an empty land with no trees and no buildings, weak in body. And He made a gourd plant grow over him, to shade him and for him to benefit from. And Allah sent him to a hundred thousand of his people or more, and they believed, so Allah let them enjoy their lives until their appointed time.

The lesson is in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿فَٱسۡتَجَبۡنَا لَهُۥ وَنَجَّيۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡغَمِّۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُـۨجِي ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'So We answered him and saved him from the distress; and thus We save the believers.' Allah saves the believers who believe truly and live by His law, and the much worship and glorification of Yunus was a cause of his rescue.

title: Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) and the Ship
description: The story of Allah's Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him), his people and the ship as the Qur'an tells it, written from al-Muyassar tafsir of its verses.

pages.text: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦٓ إِنِّي لَكُمۡ نَذِيرٞ مُّبِينٌ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'And We sent Nuh to his people: I am a clear warner to you.' He called them to worship Allah alone, and warned them of the punishment of a painful day.

The chiefs of disbelief among his people denied him and accused him of lying. Allah revealed to him that none of his people would believe except those who had already believed, and commanded him to build the ship, while he was in Allah's keeping and care. So Nuh was building the ship, and whenever a group of the chiefs of his people passed by him, they mocked him.

Then, when the command of Allah came, water gushed out strongly from the oven, a sign that the punishment had come. And Allah commanded Nuh to carry in the ship a male and a female of every kind of animal, and his household except those against whom the word had already gone forth because they did not believe, and those who believed with him. And only a few believed with him.

Nuh said to those who believed with him: ﴿ٱرۡكَبُواْ فِيهَا بِسۡمِ ٱللَّهِ مَجۡرٜىٰهَا وَمُرۡسَىٰهَآۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَغَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'Board it; in the name of Allah it sails and in the name of Allah it comes to rest. My Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.' And the ship sailed with them through waves that rose until they were like mountains.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبۡنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِي مَعۡزِلٖ يَٰبُنَيَّ ٱرۡكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'And Nuh called out to his son, who was apart: O my son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers.' His son was in a place where he had kept himself apart from the believers. But his son would not board, and the waves came between them, and he was among those who were drowned.

Then the water went down, and the ship came to rest on Mount al-Judi. Among the lessons of these verses: Nuh (peace be upon him) built the ship as Allah had commanded him, even though the chiefs of his people mocked him. Another is that on that day nothing could protect anyone from the command of Allah except those on whom Allah had mercy. And another is that all we do should be in the name of Allah, as the ship sailed and came to rest in the name of Allah.

pages.text: Allah gave Ibrahim (peace be upon him) right guidance. And Allah knew that he was worthy of it.
His father and his people worshipped idols that they had made. And Ibrahim spoke out against their worship of these statues.
When his people had gone away, Ibrahim broke the idols into small pieces. He left the biggest of them, so that they would come back to it and ask it, and their error would become clear to them.

pages.text: Allah gave Ibrahim (peace be upon him) right guidance, and He knew that he was worthy of it. And Ibrahim was calling people to this guidance.

He said to them: ﴿مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنتُمۡ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'What are these statues to which you keep devoted?' When his people had gone away, Ibrahim broke the idols into small pieces, and left the biggest of them so that they would come back to it and ask it. When they came back and saw their idols broken, they brought Ibrahim before the eyes of the people.

They turned to themselves and their error became clear to them, but soon they went back to their stubbornness. Ibrahim said to them: ﴿أَفَتَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمۡ شَيۡـٔٗا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمۡ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'Do you then worship, instead of Allah, what can neither benefit you at all nor harm you?' description: The story of Musa (peace be upon him) as a baby, as the Qur'an tells it in Surat al-Qasas, written from al-Muyassar tafsir of its verses.

pages.text: Allah inspired the mother of Musa when she gave birth to him and feared that Pharaoh would slaughter him, as he slaughtered the sons of the Children of Israel. He inspired her: ﴿أَنۡ أَرۡضِعِيهِۖ فَإِذَا خِفۡتِ عَلَيۡهِ فَأَلۡقِيهِ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِي وَلَا تَحۡزَنِيٓۖ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيۡكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'Nurse him; and when you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear and do not grieve; We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers.'

So she put him in a box and cast it into the river, the Nile. Her heart became empty of everything except worry for Musa, and she almost revealed that he was her son, had Allah not made her heart firm, so she was patient, to be one of those who believe in Allah's promise.
The box went on in the river until Pharaoh's people found it and took it. In this was Allah's decree: that Musa would become an enemy and a grief to them, and that their ruin would come through him.

When Pharaoh's wife saw him, Allah put love for him in her heart, and she said to Pharaoh: ﴿قُرَّتُ عَيۡنٖ لِّي وَلَكَۖ لَا تَقۡتُلُوهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوۡ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدٗا﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'A comfort to the eye for me and for you; do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son.' And they did not realise that their ruin would come through him.

The mother of Musa told his sister to follow his trail, and she watched him from a distance, while Pharaoh's people did not know she was his sister. Allah made Musa refuse every nurse, and his sister offered to show them a family who would raise and nurse him well, and they agreed.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿فَرَدَدۡنَٰهُ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّهِۦ كَيۡ تَقَرَّ عَيۡنُهَا وَلَا تَحۡزَنَ وَلِتَعۡلَمَ أَنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقّٞ﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'So We returned him to his mother, that she might be comforted and not grieve, and that she would know that the promise of Allah is true.' pages.text: This is the story of Allah's mercy to His servant Zakariya (peace be upon him), and in it is a lesson for those who reflect. Zakariya called on his Lord in secret, so that his du'a would be more sincere to Allah and closer to being answered.

He said in his du'a: ﴿رَبِّ إِنِّي وَهَنَ ٱلۡعَظۡمُ مِنِّي وَٱشۡتَعَلَ ٱلرَّأۡسُ شَيۡبٗا وَلَمۡ أَكُنۢ بِدُعَآئِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيّٗا﴾ — interpretation of the meaning: 'My Lord, my bones have grown weak and my hair has turned white, and I have never been let down in my du'a to You, my Lord.' His wife could not have children, so he asked his Lord to give him a child from Him, to inherit prophethood and to be pleasing.

Allah gave him glad tidings of a boy named Yahya, a name no one was given before him. Zakariya wondered how he could have a boy when he had reached the very end of old age, and his Lord told him that this was easy for Him, for He had created him before, when he was nothing. And Allah gave him a sign: that he would not be able to speak to people for three nights and their days, while he was healthy and well.
Zakariya came out to his people from his place of prayer, and signalled to them to glorify Allah morning and evening, in thanks to Him.
